Overview

Objective

  • Identify innovators and researchers.
  • Foster innovative solutions and digital advancements for sustainable mobility.
  • Focus on enhancing mass mobility, reducing environmental impact, improving road safety, and reducing accidents/fatalities.
  • Encourage ideas in connectivity, synthetic fuels, clean technologies, electrification, innovative brake systems, and inclusive mobility for persons with disabilities, senior citizens, and women.

Problem Areas & Statements

Road Hazard Detection for Safer Mobility

  • Challenge: High accident rates in rural and semi-urban India due to potholes, uneven roads, and waterlogged craters.
  • Goal: Develop a cost-effective Road Hazard Intelligence System (RHIS) integrating sensors, smartphones, cameras, telematics, ADAS, and government platforms.

Lightweight Recycled & Bio-Based Automotive Materials

  • Challenge: Automotive manufacturing is resource- and emission-intensive.
  • Goal: Create automotive-grade lightweight materials using recycled metals and bio-based composites to reduce emissions.

Assistive Mobility for Vulnerable Populations

  • Challenge: Public mobility is inaccessible for people with cognitive disabilities, autism, and elderly individuals.
  • Goal: Develop a mobility assistant enabling safe and independent transportation for these populations.

EV Charging Solutions for Rural & Semi-Urban Areas

  • Challenge: Uneven electricity access and unreliable grids limit EV adoption.
  • Goal: Create scalable, renewable energy-powered, intelligence-enabled EV charging infrastructure.

Non-Motorized Transport (NMT) Safety & Usability

  • Challenge: Pedestrians and cyclists face high fatality risk with limited infrastructure.
  • Goal: Develop cost-effective solutions to improve walking and cycling safety without requiring large infrastructure investments.

Program Structure & Rounds

Round 1 – Application Submission (Online)

  • Submit defined solution approach via official link.
  • No prototype required.
  • Deadline: 31 January 2026.

Round 2 – Phase 1: Screening & Bootcamps (4 Weeks)

  • Multi-level screening process.
  • Expert mentorship sessions.
  • Creation of a prototype development plan.

Round 3 – Phase 2: Prototyping & Incubation (12 Weeks)

  • Deep mentorship with industry leaders.
  • Access to advanced labs and infrastructure.
  • Funding: Prototyping grants up to ₹10 Lakhs (approval-based).
  • Opportunity to showcase innovations to investors and corporates at Demo Day.

Rewards & Incentives

  • Funding: Prototyping grants up to ₹10 Lakhs.
  • Mentorship: Guidance from Bosch experts, industry leaders, and domain specialists.
  • Infrastructure: Access to BMU’s advanced labs and incubator facilities.
  • Networking: Connect with investors, VCs, and funding partners.
  • Pilot Opportunities: Potential collaboration with industry partners.

Themes

Problem Area 1: Cost-effective Road Hazard Detection for Safer Mobility in Rural and Semi-Urban India.

Relevant SDGs: SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities Brief Background India’s road safety challenge remains one of the most critical mobility and public-health issues globally. Despite advances in vehicle safety, infrastructure quality particularly road hazards such as potholes, uneven road conditions, broken edges, and water-logged craters continue to be a dominant cause of accidents in rural and semi-urban regions. According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), out of the total 4.8 lakhs road accidents, and 1.72 lakhs deaths, potholes alone contributed to approximately 5,840 accidents and 2,161 deaths in 2023, highlighting a systemic failure in early detection, driver warning, and maintenance response. This gap presents requirement for a Unified Road Hazard Intelligence System (RHIS) that integrates multi-source hazard detection (vehicle sensors, smartphones, cameras, and telematics), real-time analytics, in-vehicle ADAS integration, and a government-grade platform for Public Works Department (PWD) engineers and government. Problem Statement: To develop a cost-effective, road hazard intelligence system which canhelp prevent accidents due to road anomalies.

Problem Area 2: Lightweight Recycled Materials & Bio-Based Automotive Components.

Relevant SDGs: SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production SDG 13 – Climate Action Brief Background: Automotive manufacturing is among the most resource and emission- intensive industrial sectors, driven by high material throughput, energy-intensive processing, and reliance on virgin metals and petrochemical-based composites. As vehicle electrification and efficiency improvements accelerate, material innovation has emerged as a critical, parallel lever for lifecycle emissions reduction. Lightweight recycled metals and bio-based composites offer a pathway to simultaneously reduce manufacturing emissions, improve vehicle efficiency, and strengthen supply-chain resilience aligned with India’s circular economy and net-zero manufacturing ambitions. Problem Statement: To develop an automotive-grade lightweight material using recycled metals and bio-based composites to reduce vehicular emissions.

Problem AreasRead more

Problem Area 3: Enabling Independent Mobility for People with Cognitive Disabilities, Autism, and the Elderly

Relevant SDGs: SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities Brief Background: Mobility is a fundamental enabler of dignity, independence, healthcare access, education, and economic participation. Yet for people with cognitive disabilities, autism spectrum conditions, and elderly populations, public mobility systems remain largely inaccessible, unsafe, and overwhelming, particularly in complex, high-density environments such as Indian cities. This presents the urgent need and strategic opportunity for developing an assistive mobility and navigation ecosystem tailored to these vulnerable populations. Addressing this challenge directly supports: Equity and inclusion • Road safety for vulnerable users • Access to public services • Reduced healthcare and caregiver burden Problem Statement: To develop a mobility assistant enabling safe, independent public mobility for: • People with cognitive disabilities and autism • Elderly users

Problem AreasRead more

Problem Area 4: EV Charging Stations for Rural & Semi-Urban regions: A Scalable Approach to Inclusive Electric Mobility.

Relevant SDGs: SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities SDG 13 – Climate Action Brief Background: India’s electric mobility transition is increasingly extending beyond metropolitan cities into rural and semi-urban regions, driven by electric two-wheelers, e-rickshaws, and rural logistics vehicles. However, unreliable grid infrastructure and uneven electricity access present a major barrier to equitable EV adoption. This presents an urgent need for an EV charging solutions in rural & Semi-Urban regions, and an opportunity to build a scalable, renewable energy-powered, intelligence-enabled charging ecosystem. Problem Statement: To develop an EV charging solution for rural & Semi-Urban regions.

Problem AreasRead more

Problem Area 5: Enhancing Non-Motorized Mobility (NMT) with Minimal Investment: A High-Impact, Cost-effective Opportunity for Road Safety, Health, and Climate Action in India.

Relevant SDGs: SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities SDG 13 – Climate Action Brief Background Walking and cycling constitute a substantial share of daily trips in India, particularly among low-income households, students, and elderly populations. Despite this, pedestrians and cyclists face disproportionately high fatality, and injury risks due to vehicle-centric street design, inadequate infrastructure, and weak enforcement. Here, we examine the scale and urgency of the NMT safety challenge, evaluates the current landscape of initiatives, identifies critical gaps, and argues that a cost-effective tactical, data-driven interventions can deliver outsized safety, health, and climate benefits at minimal investment. Drawing on evidence from MoRTH, IIT Delhi TRIP Centre, CEEW, WHO, and World Bank, it is found that NMT enhancements is one of the most urgent mobility interventions required today. Problem Statement: To develop a cost-effective scalable solution to improve walking and cycling safety and usability without large infrastructure investment.

Eligibility

  • Early-stage startups, innovators, researchers, and teams.
  • Open to working professionals and students (minimum age: 18).
  • Individuals or teams are eligible.
  • Startup registration is not required initially, but mandatory to receive financial support.

Rules

Program Objectives

The objective of the program is to identify potential innovators and researchers, fostering innovative solutions and digital advancements aimed at promoting sustainable mobility, including:

  • Enhancing mobility solutions for the masses
  • Reducing environmental impact
  • Ensuring road safety leading to a reduction in accidents and fatalities

The program shall encompass focus areas including, but not limited to:

  • Connectivity

  • Synthetic fuels and clean technologies

  • Electrification

  • Innovative brake systems

  • Inclusive mobility solutions for:

    • Persons with Disabilities (PWD)
    • Senior citizens
    • Women

  • Other innovative ideas and research initiatives related to sustainable mobility

1.2 Purpose of the Program

Road safety and sustainable mobility innovations need support tailored to their unique challenges with different strategies.

While funding and mentorship are crucial, these innovations also need dedicated programs focusing on long-term impact and sustainable scalability.

To drive meaningful change, these innovations require a collaborative ecosystem that prioritizes social impact alongside profitability, ensuring:

  • Safer roads
  • Sustainable mobility for the future

The program aims to create positive social impact by providing incubation support to innovations that are:

  • Relevant
  • Innovative
  • Technology-oriented

These innovations may focus on areas such as:

  • Connectivity
  • Synthetic Fuels / Clean Tech
  • Electrification
  • Innovative Brake Discs
  • Inclusive Mobility Solutions for PWD, Seniors, and Women

3. Program Structure

The program is structured into two cohorts, each consisting of two phases.

Phase 1 – 4 Weeks

  • Screening and selection of innovators
  • Bootcamps
  • Mentorship sessions
  • Expert sessions
  • Prototype development planning

Phase 2 – 12 Weeks

  • Mentorship and expert sessions from industry leaders and experts
  • Access to advanced labs
  • Access to prototyping grant up to ₹10 Lakhs
  • Opportunity to showcase innovation to industries and corporates
  • Networking opportunities with investors

4. Application and Selection Process

4.1 Entries must be submitted through the official application link only.

4.2 Incomplete, inaccurate, or late submissions will be invalid.

4.3 Both individuals and teams are eligible to apply.

4.4 A separate application must be submitted for each problem statement.

4.5 Multi-Level Screening Process

  • Initial jury evaluation based on predefined criteria
  • Only shortlisted entries will be invited for presentations
  • Final selection based on jury scores

4.6 Confidential Scoring

  • Scores will remain confidential
  • No appeals or score-related queries will be entertained
  • The committee’s decision is final and binding

5. Program Participation Guidelines and Evaluation

Participants will receive workshops on:

  • Prototyping
  • Legal structure
  • Business models
  • Marketing
  • Go-to-market (GTM)
  • Financial planning
  • Pitching

Additional participation requirements:

  • Minimum 90% attendance mandatory
  • Regular reviews and milestone tracking

Failure to comply with the program rules may result in termination, including:

  • Non-compliance
  • Misrepresentation
  • Failure to meet milestones

6. Benefit Bundle

Participants will receive:

  • Mentorship and expert sessions from industry and corporate leaders

  • Access to financial support up to ₹10 lakhs for prototype development (subject to BOSCH approval)

  • Access to advanced labs and incubator infrastructure

  • Access to startup ecosystem networks

  • Industry and investor connections

  • Support in:

    • Financial planning
    • Pitching
    • Go-to-market strategy

7. Financial Assistance

  • Prototyping grants may be provided based on BOSCH’s approval
  • Grant amount will be determined based on the actual requirement for building prototypes
  • Final approval will be provided by the Committee

Important:

Misuse of funds may result in:

  • Disqualification
  • Legal action

8. Intellectual Property (IP)

  • All intellectual property remains with the participant
  • IP disputes may result in suspension or disqualification
  • Participants indemnify organizers against IP-related claims

9. Third-Party Conflicts

  • Organizers are not responsible for disputes between participants and third parties
  • Conflicts that affect participation may result in disqualification
  • Working professionals must ensure no conflict with existing employment

10. Confidentiality

Participants must maintain confidentiality of proprietary or sensitive information during and after the program.

11. Termination

Organizers may terminate participation due to:

  • Non-compliance
  • Misrepresentation

Providing false information may result in immediate disqualification.

Voluntary Withdrawal

  • During Phase 1:

    • 15 days written notice required

  • Post Phase 1 (after receiving grants):

    • 30 days written notice
    • Subject to grant reimbursement

The organizer’s decision is final.

12. Information Verification

  • Organizers may audit and verify participant information
  • Failure to comply with program data requirements may lead to disqualification
  • Incorrect information may result in removal from the program

13. Other Terms

  • Organizers may use participant information and materials for publicity
  • Organizers are not liable for force majeure events
  • Organizers reserve the right to modify or terminate the program without prior notice

Note: The organizers reserve the right to revise the program's terms and conditions at their discretion.
